title: The lead change message stays while hovered and closes after 8 seconds
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}, in a browser window at least 1024 px wide.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Technicians {Technician-A} and {Technician-B} are active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role and Time Clock on.
    For example: {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C682425 Ana and {Technician-B} is ZZAUTOTEST C682425 Ben.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has two Approved work orders, {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2}, both led by {Technician-A}. Neither has a shift booked on the Schedule.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C682425 Toast Timing, and {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2} are S2-37431 and S2-37432.
  • You have a stopwatch, for example on your phone.
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Board View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Drag the card for {Work-order-1} from {Technician-A}'s column onto {Technician-B}'s column, let go and start the stopwatch.
  2. Keep the pointer away from the message and watch it.
  3. Drag the card for {Work-order-2} from {Technician-A}'s column onto {Technician-B}'s column and let go.
  4. Move the pointer onto the message and keep it there for 15 seconds.
  5. Move the pointer away from the message and watch it.
  6. Drag the card for {Work-order-1} from {Technician-B}'s column onto {Technician-A}'s column and let go.
  7. Click "Undo" on the message.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Work-order-1} moves to {Technician-B}'s column and the message "{Work-order-1} assigned to {Technician-B}" shows, with "Undo".
  • Step 2: the message closes on its own about 8 seconds after you let go.
  • Step 3: the message "{Work-order-2} assigned to {Technician-B}" shows.
  • Step 4: the message stays open for the whole 15 seconds.
  • Step 5: the message closes on its own after you move away.
  • Step 6: {Work-order-1} moves to {Technician-A}'s column and the message "{Work-order-1} assigned to {Technician-A}" shows.
  • Step 7: the message closes at once and {Work-order-1} goes back to {Technician-B}'s column.

Known problem (SV-11524, open; seen on staging by the designer on 19 Oct 2026): the message reads "Lead technician updated" (or "Lead technician removed") and has no Undo button. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results say, the change has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

The PRD's messages table and its Story 4 example still read "Lead technician updated" and "Lead technician removed". S4-R5 was changed on 19 Oct 2026 to the new wording and the change log says it replaces those two messages, so this case follows S4-R5; the difference is on the product owner's question list.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 66 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 19 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10043, story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician from the board or grouped table); tickets SV-11522 (Tech View) and SV-11524 (Board View)

  • S4-R16: “The lead-change toast closes on its own after 8 seconds, stays open while the pointer is over it, and closes when Undo is clicked. Other success toasts dismiss automatically, as today.”
  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) reading “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”, or “{work order number} unassigned” after removing the lead, with an Undo button. Example: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”. This replaces the standard success toast for these two messages only.”
  • S4-R32: “Undo puts the work order back exactly as it was before the change: the previous lead technician (or Unassigned), its previous place in that technician’s order, and any shifts the change cleared (removed shifts come back as they were; a shift that was ended at the moment of the change gets its original end time back). Undo is itself a lead change: it records its own audit entry (S4-R9), follows the Invoiced or Paid rule (S4-N2), and shows no shift-clearing prompt and no new toast. If Undo cannot be saved, nothing changes and the alert “Couldn’t undo the change. Please try again.” shows.”

Not yet checked against a build.

AUTOMATION: READY - EXPECT FAIL (SV-11524)
